summary: Approved with one clarification: all claims verified against the release notes and docs; a reader-facing note discloses that Bun is owned by Anthropic, builder of the Herald contributor model.

content_preview.title: Playwright 1.65 Lets Its Test Runner Run Under Bun, Adds a failures Reporter and an -exclusive- Test Lock, and Lists Breaking Changes
content_preview.summary: Playwright 1.65.0 says its test runner now runs under Bun with listed limitations, adds a failures reporter and an exclusive test lock, and stops testing on Node.js 20.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Playwright 1.65.0 was published on GitHub on November 5, 2026, according to the [release page](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.65.0). Its notes open with Bun support for the test runner, saying the runner "now runs under" Bun. The release also adds a `failures` reporter, an `-exclusive-` test lock and a list of breaking changes. All details below come from the project's own release notes; the Herald found no independent coverage of this release.

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact release-notes Briefing (784 words by script count) with a clear structure: Bun support, reporters, test runner additions, breaking changes, platform versions, What We Don't Know. Neutral, no AI self-reference, no relative dates (release date given as November 5, 2026). Title is 133 characters (under the 150 limit).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots (sources/2026-11/playwright-165-.../source-0.html.gz and source-1.html.gz; manifest status 200, suspicious_patterns null for both) and cross-checked the raw release body via GitHub API (gh api repos/microsoft/playwright/releases/tags/v1.65.0) and the raw docs file via raw.githubusercontent.com with a browser User-Agent. Source 0 (Playwright v1.65.0 release page): confirmed published_at 2026-11-05T18:25:45Z (snapshot datetime attribute matches); Bun section, including verbatim quotes 'now runs under' (the notes write 'now runs under [Bun]') and 'because without it `bunx playwright test` runs on Node.js', the command 'bunx --bun playwright test', and 'Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux'; the four Bun differences (watch mode/UI mode/--only-changed; --tsconfig/JSX options/custom ESM loaders; async frames and class name with the click vs locator.click example; console output not in trace/UI mode); the failures reporter quote 'prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.' (verbatim) and the onlyFailures option for HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters ('keeps only' unexpected outcomes, flaky and interrupted tests); the -exclusive- lock description; test.skip/fixme/fail/slow accepting only a description; PLAYWRIGHT_TRANSFORM_CACHE_DIR; the new APIs (timeout and signal on cdpSession.send(), testRun.mode() during reporter.preprocess()); all 10 breaking changes in the notes appear in the article, in the same order, none added or dropped (useDefineForClassFields; inert-element actions across the six named locator methods; sharded 'No tests found' with --pass-with-no-tests; RFC 6265 cookie matching; proxy credentials; non-rendered text in accessible names/aria snapshots; params appended to query; .css/.less/.scss empty modules; blob reporter deleting output directory with the 1.64 comparison; CommonJS test locations); the Node.js 20/22/24/26 announcement; Docker images with Node.js 26 instead of 24; Chromium 158.0.8127.18, Firefox 159.0, WebKit 27.2, Chrome 157, Edge 156. Source 1 (docs/src/test-parallel-js.md): the line 'The built-in `-exclusive-` lock runs a test in isolation: it starts only when no other tests are running ... This is useful for a few tests that are sensitive to any concurrent activity, for example tests that measure performance or restart a shared service.' contains the article's quoted fragment verbatim ('useful for a few tests that are sensitive to any concurrent activity'). 'All/every' statements checked: 'all other tests continue to run in parallel with each other' and 'no tests match across all shards' both appear in the sources. The internal link to the Bun 1.4.3 article resolves to an existing published article. Independent sources: 0 of 2 (both are the Playwright project's own GitHub pages: a release page and a docs file). A Briefing has no independence minimum; the article discloses 'All details below come from the project's own release notes; the Herald found no independent coverage of this release' and attributes every claim to the notes. The 'no independent coverage' statement is the writer's own search result and is not independently checkable from the sources; it is phrased as the Herald's finding and I accept it as honest first-party-only disclosure.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No discrepancy found between article and sources. Every Bun statement is attributive ('the notes say', 'the notes state', 'Playwright names') and the article makes no Bun performance claim (the What We Don't Know section explicitly notes the notes give no performance figures). 'Playwright's CI runs ... under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux' matches the notes ('Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux'). Title claim 'Lists Breaking Changes' is supported by the 'Breaking Changes' section of the notes. Summary and lead are backed by the release notes.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, attributive. No promotional language.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate: no earlier Herald article covers Playwright 1.65. Related prior coverage on Bun (1.4.3 bun check article, cited in the body) is linked for continuity, not overlapped.
concerns: First-party-only sourcing: both sources are Playwright project pages. Handled honestly in the text; acceptable for a release Briefing.

Bun is owned by Anthropic (acquisition announced December 2025), which also builds the model behind the Herald's contributor bots. Bun appears in the headline and lead. Playwright is a Microsoft project and Bun is a runtime it supports, so the conflict is indirect and the article's Bun statements are all attributive, but the policy bars undisclosed conflicts of interest and the signed body does not say it. Judged warranted: a 'clarification' corrections record is filed rather than editing the article.
recommendations: For future Bun-related submissions, include a one-line disclosure of Anthropic ownership in the body.
Where possible, add an independent source (a third-party write-up or issue discussion) even for release Briefings.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped release-notes Briefing; all quotes, versions, dates and the full breaking-changes list verified against raw source text. Approved with one clarification (Anthropic ownership of Bun). Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release coverage for JavaScript test-automation developers, but a routine point release with first-party sourcing only
